title: Account trajectory playbook — staged commercial asks & QBR template
content:
Purpose and scope:
This workbook is a working template for QBR-led commercial elevation conversations. Focus is on staged asks (predictable steps toward Dedicated or Private), optional premium SLA bundles, and a lightweight renewal-risk tracker that ties technical gating to commercial asks. Designed for CSMs running 30–60 minute QBRs with technical stakeholders present.

High-level approach:
1) Treat elevation as a series of small, measurable commitments (stages) rather than a single big sale.
2) Combine business metrics (latency, cost per 1M tokens, uptime) with technical readiness gates (network, SSO, data flow) to surface blockers early.
3) Use QBRs to move the account along a predictable trajectory map: Explore -> Validate -> Commit -> Migrate -> Optimize.

Staged offers ladder (example — names can be swapped):
- Stage 0: Performance baseline review (no commercial change) — deliver QBR baseline report and ops recommendations.
- Stage 1: Reserved burst capacity (2–4 week commitment, trial pricing) — low-friction pilot for predictable peaks.
- Stage 2: Dedicated pool pilot (90-day pilot, limited throughput SLA) — cost/latency forecasts and migration playbook.
- Stage 3: Dedicated commit (annual reserved capacity, custom SLA) — pricing, capacity planning, and kickoff checklist.
- Stage 4: Private deployment evaluation (VPC/on-prem POC) — security review, compliance checklist, integration plan.
- Add-on: Premium SLA package (24/7 on-call, faster RTO, longer retention for traces) — priced as an attach to Dedicated or Private.

How to use during a QBR (20–40 min segment):
- 0–5 min: Executive snapshot (ARR contribution, usage trends, one-liner health)
- 5–12 min: Technical health + friction points (token cost drivers, tail latency, errors)
- 12–20 min: Proposed staged ask for next 30–90 days + expected impact (latency, cost, reliability)
- 20–25 min: Risks/blocks and owners (security, infra, procurement)
- 25–30 min: Success criteria and next steps (POC owner, measurement plan)

QBR slide bullets (copy into deck):
- Title: Account Health & Trajectory — [Customer] — [Quarter]
- Key metrics: q/q token volume, avg tail latency P95, monthly total cost, feature adoption (chat/embeddings/rerank)
- Recent wins: latency improvements, cost savings from batching, resolved incidents
- Current friction: queueing at peaks, SSO not validated, S3 integration not encrypted at rest (example)
- Proposed 30–90d staged ask: [Stage 2 Dedicated pilot — target throughput + owner]
- Business impact estimate: -X ms p95, -Y% unit cost, +Z% availability

Renewal & risk tracker (mini table — copy into sheet):
- account_id,account_name,current_term_end,renewal_risk_score(0-100),next_staged_ask,technical_gate_status,procurement_owner
- 10021,Acme Retail,2024-09-30,72,Stage 2 pilot,network-ok;kms-pending,Procurement Team
- 10035,FintechCo,2024-12-15,28,Stage 1 reserved-burst,sso-validated;billing-ok,Finance Lead

Renewal risk score (quick heuristic):
- Start at 50
- +20 if < 90 days to term
- +15 if active incident in last 30 days
- +10 if unit cost has increased >10% q/q without clear cause
- -15 if formal pilot committed this quarter
- -10 if C-suite usage or exec sponsor engaged
(Adjust based on account nuance; record the rationale in the tracker comment field.)

Technical gating checklist (short):
- Admin access and onboarding complete (yes/no)
- SSO and SCIM validated (yes/no)
- Production KV cache behavior profiled (yes/no)
- Network egress and private peering requirement documented (yes/no)
- Data residency & encryption alignment (KMS/HSM) (yes/no)
- Load profile sample (95/99 token distribution) supplied (yes/no)

Engineering handoff template (for pilots):
- Pilot name: [Customer] Dedicated Pilot Q2
- Target throughput: [tokens/sec or req/sec], P95 target latency, duration 90 days
- Data flows: which endpoints, S3 buckets, crawl frequency
- Success metrics: stability (error rate <0.5%), cost per 1M tokens delta, observed cache hit rate
- SRE contact: [oncall@redwood.com], CSM owner: [Name]

Sample outreach cadence for staged ask conversion (6 weeks):
- Week 0: QBR — introduce staged ask + documentation pack
- Week 1: Send pilot SOW and tech kickoff invite; include draft cost delta and capacity plan
- Week 2: Technical kickoff with infra and security — close gating items (SSO/KMS)
- Week 3–4: Midpoint health check, initial performance snapshots, procurement follow-up
- Week 5: Pre-commit review — exec summary for procurement and finance
- Week 6: Commitment or next-step decision (extend pilot / escalate)

Commercial framing scripts (short):
- If procurement asks for price relief: "We structure these as staged commitments so you can test the delta in a narrow window — we’ll show measured latency and unit-cost improvements before commitments widen."
- If engineering pushes on risk: "We include a clear technical gate checklist and a rollback plan. We own the migration runbook and will run a non-prod rehearsal first."

Open questions & playbook TODOs (for this doc):
- Build a simple pricing calculator widget for CSMs to populate live during QBRs (inputs: current tokens/mo, expected delta, target P95)
- Add a short procurement-ready SOW template for Stage 2 pilots
- Collect 3 anonymized case studies with measured cost/latency delta for Dedicated pilots

Appendix: quick cost delta calculator (paste into sheet):
- current_tokens_mo,expected_delta_pct,current_cost_per_1M,expected_cost_per_1M_after
- 12, - (example row)

Notes to self (CSM roughs):
- Use customer-specific numbers when possible — generalities kill momentum.
- Flag accounts where legal security questionnaire > 40 questions — these usually need Solutions Eng earlier.
- If the account is in Europe/APAC, surface data residency up front for Private evals.

Revision history:
- 2024-03-12 initial draft by Jordan Liu
- 2024-04-01 added risk scoring heuristic (Maya Patel)
- 2024-06-10 updated staged ladder language and added sample cadence (Lars Østergaard)

End of document.
